Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir visited Turbat in Balochistan to evaluate the prevailing security situation, operational readiness, and local socio-economic development initiatives. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations, the military leader was received upon arrival by the Commander of the Balochistan Corps before paying tribute at the Martyrs’ Monument with a floral wreath and Fateha.

During the visit, the Field Marshal received a comprehensive briefing on operational readiness and ongoing counterterrorism operations targeting foreign-sponsored threats in the region. He was also updated on various socio-economic development projects designed to improve the welfare of the local population. Field Marshal Munir praised the troops for their high professionalism, operational readiness, and dedication under difficult conditions to protect the country's sovereignty.

This visit follows a previous inspection in Peshawar, where the Field Marshal and Chief of Defence Forces vowed to deliver a total defeat to terrorists and their ideology. At the Corps Headquarters in Peshawar, he reviewed border management measures and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa force readiness, urging personnel to maintain strict vigilance and the highest standards of operational preparedness against all threats.

stories.title: اسلام آباد کے قریب بنجر زمین پر انوکھا ریجینیریٹو زرعی فارم قائم
stories.summary:
اسلام آباد کے مضافات میں لہترار روڈ پر واقع سپریم کورٹ کے وکیل میاں عبدالرؤف کی ڈھائی ایکڑ بنجر زمین اب ایک سرسبز اور منافع بخش زرعی فارم میں تبدیل ہو چکی ہے۔ چار سال قبل یہ زمین محض ایک فارم ہاؤس اور شہر کی زندگی سے فرار کا ذریعہ تھی۔ اب اس سولہ کنال قابل کاشت رقبے پر پندرہ سو پھلدار درخت، چھیالیس اقسام کے پھل، موسمی اور بے موسمی سبزیاں اور سالانہ ڈھائی لاکھ سجاوٹی پھول اگائے جا رہے ہیں۔

اس فارم کو بنجر سے سرسبز بنانے والے زرعی سائنسدان اور پاکستان ایگریکلچر ریسرچ کونسل کے سابق چیئرمین ڈاکٹر محمد عظیم خان ہیں۔ انھوں نے چالیس سالہ تجربے کو بروئے کار لاتے ہوئے اس ناہموار ڈھلوان کو جدید خطوط پر ڈیزائن کیا۔ بارش کے پانی کو روکنے کے لیے ایک ڈیم نما ذخیرہ بنایا گیا ہے، جہاں سے سولر پاور کے ذریعے پانی اوپر تالاب میں پہنچایا جاتا ہے اور زیر زمین پائپ لائنوں کے ذریعے پورے فارم کو سیراب کیا جاتا ہے۔

فارم کی خاص بات یہ ہے کہ یہاں تمام فصلیں مکمل طور پر قدرتی اور ریجینیریٹو طریقوں سے اگائی جاتی ہیں، اور کسی قسم کی کیمیکل کھاد یا کیڑے مار دوا کا استعمال نہیں کیا جاتا۔ قدرتی کھاد فارم پر ہی جانوروں کے فضلے اور باقیات سے تیار کی جاتی ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ چینی طرز کی ٹنل میں بے موسمی سبزیاں اور مہنگے پھول بھی اگائے جاتے ہیں جو مارکیٹ میں جلدی آ کر اچھے دام دیتے ہیں۔

ڈاکٹر محمد عظیم کے مطابق اس بارانی اور ناہموار زمین کو اس طرح تیار کیا گیا ہے کہ یہ جلد سالانہ ستر سے اسی لاکھ روپے کمانے کے قابل ہو جائے گی۔ ان کا کہنا ہے کہ یہ ماڈل پاکستان کے ان چھوٹے کسانوں کے لیے ایک بہترین مثال ہے جن کے پاس زمین کم ہے۔ فارم کے مالک میاں عبدالرؤف کے مطابق اب یہ فارم اپنے اخراجات خود اٹھانے کے قابل ہو چکا ہے۔

stories.title: Bangladesh Deploys Paramilitary Forces Amid Unrest Over Hasina's Return
stories.summary:
Bangladesh increased security and deployed hundreds of paramilitary troops nationwide following a wave of clashes, bomb blasts, and arson attacks. The unrest was triggered by plans from former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who has lived in exile in India since fleeing violent protests in August 2024, to return in December. The government has rejected her passport and identity card requests, prompting members and supporters of her banned Awami League party to stage street protests and a week-long mobilization culminating in a planned nationwide lockdown on November 19.

Over the past ten days, police have recorded crude bomb blasts and vehicle arson across at least 28 districts, injuring multiple civilians and police personnel. Incidents include the fatal burning of a bus company helper in Pirojpur, the death of a ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party activist near Hasina's home district of Gopalganj, and arson attacks targeting homes, shops, and at least 37 branches of the Grameen Bank. The bank was founded by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, who led the interim government after Hasina's ouster.

Tuesday marked the one-year anniversary of a local court sentencing Hasina to death for ordering a deadly crackdown on the 2024 student-led uprising. The current government, led by the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, has blamed the banned Awami League for the ongoing violence. In response to the escalation, Dhaka Metropolitan Police arrested at least 71 members of banned organizations over a 24-hour period, according to police spokesperson Niaz Mehedi.

The deployment of security forces aims to restore order amid deep political polarization surrounding Hasina's potential return. The situation remains tense as authorities counter property destruction, targeted arson against financial institutions, and violent clashes across multiple districts.

stories.title: Pakistan Approves PPP Model for Two Sections of M-6 Motorway
stories.summary:
The Public Private Partnership Authority board in Islamabad approved constructing two sections of the Hyderabad-Sukkur Motorway, known as M-6, through a public-private partnership model. Chaired by Privatisation Commission Chairman and Prime Minister's Adviser Muhammad Ali, the board decided that contracts for sections I and II of the 121-kilometer stretch will be awarded via separate concession agreements. This initiative aims to complete Pakistan's north-south motorway corridor and attract private funding for infrastructure development.

Private investors will develop and operate each section for 25 years, recovering costs through toll revenues before returning the motorway to the National Highway Authority in good condition. The government will provide Viability Gap Funding exclusively for Section I to ensure commercial viability and keep user tolls affordable. The Asian Development Bank serves as the transaction adviser for the National Highway Authority, which will soon invite bids from qualified local and international investors.

The entire M-6 project is planned as a 306-kilometer, six-lane, access-controlled highway divided into five sections. Upon completion, it is expected to reduce travel time between Hyderabad and Sukkur from roughly six hours to three hours. Currently, all traffic relies on the crowded N-5 National Highway, where heavy freight vehicles share narrow roads through towns, presenting significant road-safety concerns.

stories.title: Red Cross Urges Ban on Lethal Autonomous Weapons at UN Talks
stories.summary:
A weapons expert from the International Committee of the Red Cross warned against the dangers of lethal autonomous weapons during United Nations talks in Geneva. Laurent Gisel, head of the ICRC weapons unit, emphasized the urgent need for binding rules before unpredictable and unmanageable weapons are deployed widely. Countries gathered at the UN Review Conference of the High Contracting Parties to the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons to discuss regulations for these systems, often called killer robots.

While automated defense systems like warship missile interceptors have existed for decades with human oversight, rapid artificial intelligence advancements have introduced offensive weapons designed to autonomously seek and destroy targets. Gisel highlighted loitering munitions as a key concern because they can search for enemy radars and dive to destroy them, risking detonations near civilian infrastructure. Such outcomes conflict with international humanitarian law, which mandates distinguishing between civilians and combatants, and between military targets and civilian facilities.

The ICRC is not seeking to ban all automation, but advocates prohibiting unpredictable autonomous weapons and systems designed to directly target humans. Gisel criticized weapons that reduce humans to data processed by algorithms, noting that machine processes ultimately decide life and death. Furthermore, he highlighted risks regarding changing battlefield conditions, such as a combatant surrendering or becoming wounded after a weapon is activated, thereby gaining protected legal status.

stories.title: Exchange Rate Relevance Questioned Amid Industrial Silence in Pakistan
stories.summary:
Economic discussions in Pakistan frequently debate whether the currency should be devalued to enhance export competitiveness, often pointing to the Real Effective Exchange Rate. The REER measures a country's exchange rate against the inflation-adjusted rates of its main trading partners, with a reading above 100 signaling an overvalued currency that makes exports expensive. Despite the REER staying above its equilibrium level for months, exporter associations and chambers of commerce have remained publicly silent on the exchange rate, choosing instead to focus complaints on interest rates, taxation, and utility prices.

Similarly, a proposed new auto policy aimed at gradually reducing import tariffs has drawn fierce opposition from auto parts manufacturers represented by PAAPAM, who argue their investments are threatened. However, major vehicle assembly companies have remained quiet because the policy changes do not adversely affect their business interests. Analysts note that exporters are not demanding devaluation and automakers are not asking for old protections because current market conditions do not make those measures pressing concerns for them.

Policymakers historically base exchange rate decisions on external debt servicing requirements and maintaining State Bank liquid reserves rather than export competitiveness. Current market conditions show an abundant supply of dollars, no flight into foreign currency, and an interbank market where banks finance imports from inflows while the central bank builds reserves. Under these circumstances, economists view immediate currency devaluation as unlikely until forced by concrete market realities.

stories.title: Pat Cummins Defiant as Sandpapergate Scandal Revives Captaincy Scrutiny
stories.summary:
Australian Test cricket captain Pat Cummins remained defiant on Thursday amid intense pressure regarding his leadership after being dragged back into the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal. The controversy resurfaced following explosive revelations in a newspaper column by Cameron Bancroft, a central figure in the Cape Town incident, who claimed that the entire team was aware of the plot. Bancroft expressed feeling angry and betrayed by Cummins' recent denials, specifically pointing to a 70-minute press conference in Sydney where the captain forcefully rebutted similar allegations made by Usman Khawaja.

Neil Maxwell, Cummins' manager, released a statement defending the captain, maintaining that his position has stayed consistent over the past eight years and emphasizing his role in rebuilding the Australian cricket team. Despite this defense, prominent media outlets, including The Australian, ABC, and the Sydney Morning Herald, published opinion pieces questioning Cummins' future and stating that his captaincy is in peril. In response to the unfolding situation, Cricket Australia delayed the announcement of the squad for the upcoming home Test series against New Zealand.

Cricket Australia Chief Executive Todd Greenberg declared that Cummins' version of events is not under scrutiny and announced that the board would establish a forum for players to share their 2018 experiences rather than reopen the investigation. Meanwhile, Bancroft made further accusations, alleging that David Warner first brought up using sandpaper during the second Test at Port Elizabeth and that coaches Darren Lehmann and David Saker were present during the discussions. Lehmann, who resigned shortly after the 2018 scandal, consistently denied any prior knowledge and stated he needed time to process the new allegations.

The 2018 ball-tampering plot initially resulted in severe sanctions, with Bancroft, Steve Smith, and David Warner being sent home in disgrace and handed bans after an official Cricket Australia probe found them responsible. Although Bancroft previously hinted in a 2021 interview that the bowling group knew about the scheme—prompting public denials from Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, and Nathan Lyon—the latest claims have reignited calls for a review of the current Test captain. The unfolding saga continues to cast a long shadow over Australian cricket as officials and players grapple with the renewed controversy.

stories.title: Pakistan Experiences Quiet Solar Revolution Driven by Ordinary Citizens
stories.summary:
At COP31, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif highlighted an extraordinary energy transition in Pakistan, noting that ordinary citizens have installed nearly 22 gigawatts of rooftop solar capacity over a two-year period in search of affordable electricity. This quiet revolution occurred largely without state planning, driven instead by escalating capacity payments, a falling rupee, and IMF-backed reforms that removed hidden subsidies and caused base tariffs to double between fiscal year 2022 and 2025. Concurrently, cheap Chinese solar panels flooded the market while persistent loadshedding pushed households and businesses toward self-generation.

The widespread adoption of distributed solar has yielded substantial economic and environmental dividends. According to estimates by Ember, CREA, and Renewables First, rooftop solar installations avoided over $12 billion in oil and gas imports by February 2026, with an additional $6.3 billion expected this year, alongside roughly 35 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions avoided in fiscal year 2025. Accounting for grid losses, solar power now supplies about one-third of the nation's electricity, while operating 52 percent of the country's 1.83 million agricultural irrigation pumps largely independently of state assistance. Transport has also seen shifts, with electric motorcycles accounting for over one in 10 vehicle sales this year.

Experts argue that transitioning past the initial phase of rooftop installations requires a strategic second phase focused on enhanced storage, fair grid tariffs, accelerated electric vehicle adoption, and solar mini-grids for the millions still lacking electricity. Furthermore, climate experts emphasize the urgent need to address agricultural water and resource management, noting that subsidized solar pumping and low canal water charges have driven the expansion of water-intensive crops like rice and sugarcane, leading to declining water tables and increased methane and nitrous oxide emissions. Proposed reforms include conditional solarisation requiring efficient irrigation, volumetric water and crop pricing, targeted fertilizer support tied to soil testing, alternate wetting and drying methods for rice cultivation, and satellite-enforced residue burning rules.

Funding these comprehensive adaptation measures could potentially rely on domestic revenue streams, such as record petroleum levies and budgeted climate support funds, alongside provincial budget surpluses. While the IMF's existing Resilience and Sustainability Facility incorporates irrigation pricing, deeper structural benchmarks could officially integrate water adaptation into future programs. By proactively designing the next phase of resource and energy management, Islamabad can build long-term national resilience, secure further concessional climate financing, and build upon the unexpected successes of the initial solar energy transition.

stories.title: Trump Calls Historic Trilateral Summit With Xi and Putin a Win
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump stated that his upcoming meeting in Shenzhen with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin was already a success before it officially commenced, greeting a warm reception in China. The unprecedented diplomatic gathering brings together the leaders of the world's largest nuclear-armed nations, though analysts suggest it is unlikely to yield major agreements and has caused unease among smaller countries fearing their interests might be sidelined. Trump contrasted his lavish welcome ceremony—featuring Xi greeting him personally at the airport alongside traditional pageantry, children, and soldiers—with the more muted arrivals of other global leaders.

The trilateral event follows pointed remarks delivered by Xi and Putin ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. In a prior speech, Xi advocated for free and open trade, positioning Beijing as a stable alternative to the United States and its recent tariff hikes and assertive foreign policy under Trump. Meanwhile, Trump and Putin exchanged a brief handshake and a few words during a photo opportunity where they flanked Xi, though no full-scale bilateral talks were scheduled for their individual pull-aside meeting. Trump has repeatedly emphasized nuclear arms control as a primary agenda item for the summit, despite China's consistent refusal to join bilateral reduction frameworks established by Washington and Moscow.

Ahead of the main gathering, Trump planned to hold discussions and a working lunch with Xi to evaluate the durability of a recent trade truce. This economic dialogue unfolds amid ongoing bilateral friction regarding export curbs and reports of advanced Nvidia chips being illicitly diverted to China through Southeast Asia. Regarding international conflicts, Trump asserted that the United States did not require assistance from Russia or China to resolve the situation in Iran, pointing to prior military actions against Iranian naval and aerial forces, while White House officials indicated that the ongoing war in Ukraine was not expected to be a formal discussion point.

Trump's broader Asia trip serves as an opportunity to project American influence, reinforce regional alliances, and engage in high-profile diplomacy with key geopolitical rivals. However, the US president returns to domestic challenges upon the conclusion of the trip, including the fallout from midterm legislative elections and recent technological and aviation service disruptions across the United States. While the three leaders found strategic utility in appearing together for a unified photograph, policy experts note that substantive alignment across deeply divided issues such as trade, regional security, and military modernization remains a significant hurdle.

stories.title: Jasprit Bumrah Shines on Test Return as New Zealand Reaches 140-5
stories.summary:
Jasprit Bumrah made a sensational return to Test cricket on Thursday, claiming 3 wickets for 31 runs to help India restrict New Zealand to 140 for 5 at tea on the opening day of the first Test in Wellington. Playing his first red-ball international in a year, the Indian paceman struck with only his third delivery of the day, removing New Zealand captain Tom Latham for a duck. The Basin Reserve pitch offered favorable conditions for the seamers early on after Indian skipper Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bowl.

New Zealand stumbled early when Anshul Kamboj—selected as a surprise inclusion over Mohammed Siraj—had Devon Conway caught behind for 4, leaving the hosts struggling at 12 for 2 within four overs. Rachin Ravindra then contributed 15 runs alongside Henry Nicholls before edging an Akash Deep delivery behind. Bumrah returned for a second spell before lunch to remove Daryl Mitchell for 1 with a sharp catch taken by Yashasvi Jaiswal at short leg, and subsequently dismissed Tom Blundell for 5 shortly after the interval.

Despite the early collapse, New Zealand's batters stabilized as the surface eased. Henry Nicholls anchored the innings with a resilient knock, reaching 66 not out by the second break to build upon his history of four previous Test centuries at the venue. He was joined at the crease by Glenn Phillips, who remained unbeaten on 42, as the pair safely navigated through an unbroken 70-run partnership for the sixth wicket. The second and final Test of the series is scheduled to begin in Christchurch on November 27.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Faces Hawkish Fed Signals Amid Strong Equity Inflows
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee is anticipated to open largely flat on Thursday following a previous close of 93.44 against the US dollar. Despite touching a seven-month high of 93.2450 during the preceding session before pulling back, the currency's upward trajectory continues to be supported by sustained foreign equity inflows and cautious market positioning where speculators are hesitant to hold long dollar bets.

Domestic equities saw cooling momentum on Wednesday, yet foreign investors maintained strong buying activity by injecting over $600 million into local shares. This latest influx pushes total net purchases by foreign investors for the month to nearly $12 billion. Currency traders note that while the downward bias on the USD/INR pair remains intact, further gains for the rupee are expected to occur at a gradual, incremental pace interspersed with periods of market consolidation.

Meanwhile, the rupee's recovery confronts external pressures from shifting United States monetary policy expectations. Minutes from the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting indicated heightened concern among policymakers regarding persistent inflation, with several officials advocating for additional policy tightening. These hawkish signals were reinforced by Fed Governor Christopher Waller, who suggested a potential 50-basis-point rate hike in December or accelerated increases in 2027. Consequently, Danske Bank has updated its outlook to project a January rate hike alongside three subsequent 25-basis-point increases, which would lift the federal funds rate to a range of 4.50% to 4.75%.

stories.title: Oil Prices Hold Steady as Supply Surplus Fears Offset Conflict Risks
stories.summary:
Oil prices remained steady on Thursday following a previous decline, as growing expectations of a global supply surplus and higher interest rates weighed on market sentiment, counterbalancing ongoing supply risks stemming from Middle East conflicts. Brent crude futures edged up by 17 cents, or 0.18%, to reach $92.12 a barrel, whereas US West Texas Intermediate futures dipped 9 cents, or 0.11%, down to $83.17 a barrel.

The previous session saw Brent drop 1.3% and WTI fall to its lowest level since August 26, driven by perceptions that crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have largely recovered to pre-war volumes. Furthermore, anticipated US interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve have strengthened the US dollar, making dollar-denominated commodities more expensive for buyers using other currencies. Minutes from the Fed's October meeting bolstered expectations of a December rate increase, while US crude inventories unexpectedly expanded by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels for the week ending November 13, according to the Energy Information Administration.

Despite economic headwinds, significant geopolitical supply risks persist in the Middle East and Eastern Europe. Iranian media reported that three oil tankers operating east of the Strait of Hormuz were disabled by underwater mines. Additionally, ongoing disruptions from the conflicts involving Russia and Iran continue to impact global energy infrastructure, with Ukrainian drone attacks having reportedly reduced Russian oil refinery crude processing volumes by 45% since late October.

stories.title: Trump calls historic trilateral summit with Xi and Putin a win
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump described his meeting in Shenzhen with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Putin as a diplomatic victory even before it commenced. The unprecedented gathering of leaders from the world's major nuclear powers received a grand welcome from Beijing, though analysts noted that major agreements were unlikely to emerge and smaller nations expressed concern that their interests might be ignored.

Trump praised the pageantry and respect shown upon his arrival, contrasting it with the more muted greetings given to other leaders. Ahead of the trilateral event, Xi and Putin delivered speeches preceding an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Xi advocated for free and open trade, positioning Beijing as a stable partner against US tariff increases and foreign policy changes. Meanwhile, Trump and Putin exchanged a brief handshake before a photo opportunity, following their previous meeting in Alaska in 2025 that failed to resolve the war in Ukraine.

The discussions touched upon nuclear arms control, with Trump highlighting the difficulty of reducing large nuclear arsenals. White House officials indicated that Trump was not expected to raise the Ukraine conflict during the talks, and Trump stated in a Fox News interview that he would not seek assistance from Russia and China to conclude the Iran conflict, asserting that US forces had already defeated Iran's military capabilities.

The talks also provided an opportunity to examine a recent trade truce between the US and China. Discussions involved concerns regarding Nvidia chips being diverted to China through Southeast Asia, which has heightened tensions over export controls and Chinese access to advanced technology.

stories.title: Suparco warns of worsening smog across Punjab as Lahore tops pollution charts
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco) has issued a warning regarding worsening smog conditions across Punjab over a three-day period. Satellite observations recorded 690 active fire incidents across Punjab and nearby transboundary areas in a 24-hour window, covering 36 districts utilizing VIIRS and MODIS satellite data. High or severe smog conditions were identified in seven districts, including Jhang, Narowal, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Gujranwala, and Dera Ghazi Khan.

While tropospheric nitrogen dioxide levels were lower than historical averages for the period, atmospheric conditions were projected to deteriorate further. The Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service model estimated particulate matter PM2.5 concentrations between 51 and 71 micrograms per cubic metre, with poor atmospheric dispersion trapping pollutants close to the ground. Concurrently, the Pakistan Meteorological Department forecast fog and smog during mornings and nights across multiple areas without significant rainfall expected.

Amid these conditions, Lahore ranked as the world's most polluted major city on Wednesday morning according to IQAir, registering an Air Quality Index reading of 339 before fluctuating throughout the day. Other Pakistani cities also recorded hazardous air quality levels, with Faisalabad topping the national list with an AQI of 686. Several cities including Gujranwala, Multan, and Kasur also registered hazardous readings above 300.

In response to the crisis, the Punjab Environment Protection Agency deployed five senior directors to supervise anti-stubble burning operations and coordinate with local administrations. Additionally, the Multan district administration deployed modern anti-smog gun vehicles to spray water continuously across the city under directives from Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz.

stories.title: Trump says he briefly mentioned ex-Nvidia boss Huang to Xi
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump stated that he briefly referenced former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during artificial intelligence discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The conversation occurred during talks between the two leaders, which included a dinner discussion focusing on artificial intelligence.

Jensen Huang resigned from his position following disclosures about extramarital affairs, which included a relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang. US intelligence agencies have been investigating Alice Huang's potential connections to China's security ministry and the nature of any information she may have accessed. When questioned about whether the affair presented a national security threat, Trump stated he had not heard reports of her acting as a spy.

Trump referred to Jensen Huang's situation as a tragedy because of his brilliance, explaining that the topic came up only briefly during his interactions with Xi. Prior to his resignation, Jensen Huang had met with Trump multiple times and expressed support for the administration's artificial intelligence agenda as Nvidia pursued chip sales to China.

stories.title: Indian shares expected to open lower following hawkish Fed minutes
stories.summary:
Indian equities are positioned for a lower opening as a hawkish stance in the latest US Federal Reserve policy minutes counters optimism driven by declining crude oil prices and continuous foreign fund inflows. GIFT Nifty futures indicated a negative start for the Nifty 50 index following its previous close at 25,227.95 points.

The October minutes from the US central bank revealed that policymakers recognized a necessity to strengthen efforts against inflation while opting to maintain current interest rates. According to Enrich Money CEO Ponmudi R, the minutes suggest further rate hikes could occur, with some policymakers contemplating increases exceeding 25 basis points in December, prompting investor caution regarding US monetary policy.

Higher interest rates in the United States tend to boost the appeal of the dollar and US Treasuries for foreign portfolio investors, potentially redirecting capital away from emerging market equities. Despite this risk, foreign portfolio investors have been net buyers in India during the month, purchasing shares worth 58.67 billion rupees ($627.69 million) on a single day and bringing their total monthly purchases to a record $11.28 billion following heavy selling over the prior two years.

Meanwhile, Brent crude futures traded around $92.5 per barrel, marking a 21.5 percent decline for the month. In broader Asian markets, the MSCI index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan remained relatively stable as chatbot developer Anthropic prepared for its market debut following a large initial public offering.

stories.title: Asian Stocks and US Futures Rise on Anthropic $81B IPO
stories.summary:
Asian equities and US stock futures advanced as Claude chatbot creator Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, securing an $81 billion offering. This valuation brings the company to approximately $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, positioning it as the first major frontier artificial intelligence model developer to go public. The upcoming market debut serves as a critical test for investor sentiment regarding the artificial intelligence sector, which has faced recent pressures and valuation concerns.

Investor confidence has been rattled by questions surrounding the profitability of artificial intelligence and the heavy debt required to build necessary infrastructure. These anxieties persisted despite a robust forecast from chipmaker Nvidia, whose market standing was further complicated by the departure of CEO Jensen Huang following his resignation last week. Regional markets presented mixed results, with Japan's Nikkei rising 1 percent, while South Korea's Kospi remained flat and Taiwan stocks dipped 1 percent, leaving the broader MSCI index for Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan down 0.3 percent.

Meanwhile, currency markets responded to hawkish remarks from US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller, who suggested the central bank take aggressive action against inflation through either a half-point rate increase in December or explicit signals for future hikes. Traders are currently pricing in a 90 percent chance of a 25 basis point rate hike next month, pushing the US dollar near its highest level since April 2025 and keeping the euro subdued at $1.0978.

In commodities, oil prices experienced downward pressure due to expectations of a growing market surplus. Brent crude futures slipped 0.58 percent to $91.47 a barrel, putting the commodity on track for its third consecutive weekly decline. Financial analysts note that while hawkish Federal Reserve policies continue to support the US dollar, the broader market mood remains fragile as investors monitor both macroeconomic tightening and the performance of technology listings.

stories.title: US Dollar Holds Near 19-Month High Amid Fed Rate Hike Signals
stories.summary:
The US dollar remained close to a 19-month high following Federal Reserve meeting minutes and hawkish commentary pointing toward potential interest rate hikes. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller indicated the central bank might need to raise rates by 50 basis points in December or signal faster tightening in 2027 to control inflation. This firm stance supported the greenback even as technology shares struggled, including chipmaker Nvidia, which faced volatility following the sudden departure of co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO last week.

Simultaneously, the Australian dollar dropped to a 10-month low of $0.6692 after official data showed employment falling for a second consecutive month in October and the jobless rate climbing to a five-year high. The weak economic figures reinforced beliefs that Australian interest rates have peaked. The strong US dollar also weighed heavily on other major currencies, pushing the euro near its lowest level since April 2025 at $1.0977 and leaving sterling near a one-month low at $1.3152, while the Japanese yen hovered near the 160 level at 159.39.

In the bond and commodity markets, US Treasuries rallied following a solid 20-year auction, lowering the 10-year yield by about 4 basis points to 5.06 percent. Falling oil prices contributed to easing inflation concerns, with US crude and fuel inventories posting larger-than-expected increases according to the Energy Information Administration. Consequently, Brent and US oil benchmarks settled down more than 1 percent on Wednesday. Gold also stabilized at $3,743 an ounce after experiencing a sharp selloff driven by the initial hawkish signals from the central bank.

Beyond monetary policy and market indicators, investors are closely watching the upcoming stock market debut of artificial intelligence firm Anthropic as a gauge for sector sentiment. Additionally, geopolitical events are drawing attention as US President Donald Trump prepares to conclude his Asia trip with a meeting alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss nuclear arms control.

stories.title: Pakistan Projected to Surpass Indonesia as Largest Muslim Nation by 2070
stories.summary:
A recent study published by the US-based Pew Research Centre indicates that Muslims are anticipated to surpass Christians as the primary global religious group by the year 2035. According to the report, titled "The Future of World Religions: Population Growth Projections, 2020-2070", the worldwide Muslim population is forecast to expand by 80 percent between 2020 and 2070, outpacing the projected 30 percent increase for Christians. Researchers attribute this rapid growth primarily to higher fertility rates and a younger average demographic within Muslim populations, noting that Muslim women had an average of 3.1 children during the 2020 to 2025 period compared to 2.5 for Christian women.

Globally, the total Muslim population is estimated to grow from 2.02 billion in 2020 to 3.64 billion by 2070, making up approximately 36 percent of the world's population. In contrast, the global Christian population is expected to reach nearly 2.96 billion, accounting for about 29 percent of the total by 2070. The study highlights significant changes in the geographical distribution of these populations over the decades.

Notably, Pakistan is projected to replace Indonesia as the home of the world's largest Muslim population by 2070. Pakistan's Muslim population is expected to nearly double, rising from 227 million in 2020 to approximately 461 million in 2020's forecast end-point of 2070. A corresponding demographic shift is anticipated among Christians, with the Democratic Republic of the Congo expected to surpass the United States to hold the largest Christian population by the same year.

The Pew Research Centre study examined demographic trends across 201 countries and territories, factoring in age structures, fertility rates, mortality, migration, and religious switching. The organization noted that the projections rely on the continuation of recent trends and do not account for external disruptions such as wars, natural disasters, epidemics, or significant economic and social shifts.

stories.title: Sindh Governor and Austrian Envoy Discuss Expanding Bilateral Trade
stories.summary:
Sindh Governor Syed Muhammad Nehal Hashmi and Austrian Ambassador Wolfgang Oliver Kutschera met at the Governor House to explore avenues for expanding bilateral trade, enhancing investment, and deepening economic cooperation between Pakistan and Austria. The discussion centered on identifying new commercial engagements, joint ventures, and industrial cooperation across multiple sectors to strengthen long-standing friendly relations between the two nations.

During the meeting, Governor Hashmi emphasized the importance of translating traditional diplomatic ties into robust economic partnerships. He highlighted the need to facilitate technology transfer, boost exports and imports, and encourage direct business collaborations. He pointed to renewable energy, hydropower, infrastructure, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and industrial machinery as promising areas where Austria's expertise matches Pakistan's market potential. The talks also acknowledged existing trade patterns, noting that Pakistan exports textiles, footwear, and fabrics to Austria while importing pharmaceutical machinery, exploration equipment, cable cars, chemicals, hydropower technology, and products such as Red Bull.

Both officials agreed to empower the Pakistan-Austria Joint Committee to foster direct communication between trade organizations, investors, and business communities. Ambassador Kutschera expressed a strong interest in pursuing further investment within Pakistan and praised the local culture, hospitality, and the city of Karachi, which he described as a "Mini Pakistan" following an enjoyable visit.

Several key officials attended the meeting alongside the Governor and the Ambassador, including Austrian Honorary Consul General Dr Hussain Islam, Principal Secretary Dr Syed Saif-ur-Rehman, and Press Secretary Faisal Farooqi. Governor Hashmi concluded that increased diplomatic engagement and economic collaboration would unlock vital investment opportunities and mutually benefit both countries.

stories.title: Punjab Government Allocates Rs7.77 Billion for New WASA Machinery
stories.summary:
The Punjab government is investing Rs7.77 billion to procure modern machinery and equipment for 22 newly established Water and Sanitation Agencies across the province. Provincial Minister for Housing Bilal Yasin announced the initiative during a visit to the Millat Tractors Machinery Plant, where he inspected the production of the civil equipment designed to bolster drainage, sewerage infrastructure, and emergency response capabilities.

The comprehensive equipment package comprises 415 units of modern machinery, with deliveries scheduled for completion by March 2027. The procurement features 85 tractors, 74 suction machines, 52 jetting machines, 48 desilting machines, 71 dewatering sets, 31 dump trucks, 41 water bowsers, 10 truck-mounted cranes, and three wheeled excavators. Minister Bilal noted that establishing WASAs in all 41 districts under Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has significantly enhanced provincial sanitation management and service delivery.

The new machinery will be distributed to numerous districts throughout the province to improve operational readiness and emergency management, particularly during the monsoon season. Targeted areas include Kasur, Chiniot, Khanewal, Bahawalnagar, Muzaffargarh, Mandi Bahauddin, Pakpattan, Chakwal, Vehari, Wazirabad, Layyah, Lodhran, Attock, Khushab, Bhakkar, and Rajanpur. Millat Tractors CEO Rahil Asghar and WASA Director General Tayyab Fareed were also present at the inspection event.

stories.title: کراچی میں ریگل چوک کے قریب دکانوں میں آتشزدگی، فائر بریگیڈ کی کارروائی جاری
stories.summary:
کراچی کے علاقے ریگل چوک کے قریب چند دکانوں میں اچانک آگ بھڑک اٹھی۔ واقعے کی اطلاع ملتے ہی فائر بریگیڈ کا عملہ فوری طور پر موقع پر پہنچ گیا اور آگ پر قابو پانے کے لیے امدادی کارروائیاں شروع کر دیں۔ فائر بریگیڈ حکام کے مطابق اس وقت تین فائر ٹینڈرز اور ایک واٹر باوزر آگ بجھانے کے عمل میں بھرپور حصہ لے رہے ہیں۔

ابھی تک دکانوں میں لگنے والی اس آگ کی اصل وجوہات سامنے نہیں آ سکیں اور حکام اس معاملے کی تحقیقات کر رہے ہیں۔ واقعے کے نتیجے میں ہونے والے مالی نقصان یا کسی جانی نقصان کے بارے میں ابتدائی طور پر تفصیلات جاری نہیں کی گئی ہیں جبکہ فائر فائٹرز آگ کو مکمل طور پر بجھانے کی کوششوں میں مصروف ہیں۔

اس واقعے کے ساتھ ساتھ ملک بھر سے دیگر سیاسی اور انتظامی امور کی خبریں بھی سامنے آئی ہیں جن میں پاکستان پیپلز پارٹی کے چیئرمین بلاول بھٹو زرداری کا چھ ماہ کے اندر عام انتخابات کرانے کا مطالبہ بھی شامل ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ دیگر قومی امور پر بھی مختلف رہنماؤں کے بیانات سامنے آئے ہیں۔

حکام کی جانب سے ریگل چوک کے قریب آگ پر قابو پانے کی کوششیں آخری اطلاعات تک جاری تھیں۔ انتظامیہ کا کہنا ہے کہ کولنگ کا عمل مکمل ہونے کے بعد ہی اصل نقصان کا تخمینہ لگایا جا سکے گا اور آتشزدگی کی وجہ کا تعین کیا جائے گا۔

stories.title: Punjab Governor Stresses Public Will in New Province Debates
stories.summary:
Punjab Governor Sardar Saleem Haider Khan emphasized that public opinion is vital regarding the establishment of new provinces, noting that residents in Sindh do not support dividing their region. He highlighted that the Sindh Assembly unanimously passed a resolution against creating new administrative units, contrasting it with Punjab where similar assembly resolutions have already been pursued. Speaking at the Governor House in Lahore during a food package distribution event for primary school children, the governor stated that Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari maintains nothing should be forced onto citizens against their desires.

Governor Khan stressed that the government must supply proper educational and healthcare infrastructure to citizens. He mentioned that nutritious meals are being delivered to two schools located inside the Lahore Governor House through a welfare partner, and plans are underway to elevate the existing vocational training center into an advanced facility. He also reaffirmed that the Pakistan Peoples Party focuses its platform on basic essentials like bread, clothing, and shelter.

Addressing reporters, the governor reiterated that the political context in Sindh differs entirely from Punjab. He noted that Bilawal Bhutto Zardari advocates for systemic improvements while upholding the principle that no decision can be forced upon the public without their consent. The event underscored administrative welfare efforts alongside ongoing national political discourse regarding provincial boundaries.

Understanding these regional stances matters because debates over administrative divisions highlight deep political sensitivities across Pakistan's federating units. The governor's remarks clarify the ruling party's approach to respecting provincial autonomy and legislative consensus, particularly in maintaining stability between different regional governments.

stories.title: Pakistan Sugar Mills Association Demands Transparent Export Policy
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Sugar Mills Association (PSMA) has called on the government to establish a consistent, automated policy for exporting surplus sugar to prevent recurring financial pressures. PSMA Chairman Asim Ghani Usman stated that the country produced approximately 7.7 million tonnes of sugar during the 2025-26 crushing season. After satisfying domestic needs, an unsold surplus of 1.3 million tonnes remains, though authorities have permitted the export of only 200,000 tonnes so far. The association requested immediate approval to export at least 1 million tonnes of this surplus to generate about $500 million in foreign exchange.

According to the PSMA, sugarcane cultivation expanded by roughly 16 percent for the upcoming period, with production expected to reach 8.5 million tonnes in the 2026-27 crushing season. This increase could drive surplus stocks up to 2.7 million tonnes next year. The association warned that storing upcoming supplies will prove difficult without clearing current stocks, which could cause cash flow shortages and delay payments to sugarcane farmers, ultimately threatening rural law and order.

The industry body proposed exporting between 150,000 and 200,000 tonnes monthly once permits are issued, while allowing the government to halt shipments if domestic market conditions require it. Furthermore, the PSMA urged swift deregulation of the sugar sector, implementation of earlier export facilitation decisions, and appropriate schedule adjustments for the start of the crushing season.

Addressing these demands is crucial for stabilizing Pakistan's sugar industry, avoiding grower unrest, and protecting foreign exchange reserves. Transparent export frameworks help mills manage mounting production costs and prevent inventory logjams that threaten agricultural supply chains.

stories.title: PCDMA Expresses Concern Over FBR Tax System Restructuring Plans
stories.summary:
Pakistan Chemicals and Dyes Merchants Association (PCDMA) Chairman Saleem Mukati has voiced strong concerns regarding the Federal Board of Revenue's initiative to separate federal excise duties and sales tax from income tax administration. While acknowledging that the reorganisation and reassignment of 54 senior officers aim to enhance collection efficiency, Mukati warned that such restructuring risks heightening the tax compliance burden for businesses in Karachi and across the country.

According to the PCDMA chief, fragmenting the tax administration will compel enterprises to interact with multiple tax offices. This division is expected to generate extra documentation, repeated visits, procedural delays, and slower resolution times for grievances. Businesses are already grappling with elevated taxation, high operational costs, liquidity constraints, and intricate regulations, making a fragmented system particularly damaging for small and medium enterprises and traders.

Mukati cautioned that the split could provoke confusion concerning jurisdictions, reporting procedures, audits, refunds, and grievance redressal. Inadequate coordination between newly appointed sales tax commissioners and existing income tax authorities may produce overlapping notices and conflicting interpretations. Furthermore, he noted that frequent administrative changes risk disrupting business operations and creating uncertainty among taxpayers who are already navigating a challenging economic environment.

To mitigate these risks, Mukati urged the FBR to clearly define responsibilities and reporting structures while ensuring seamless coordination among income tax, sales tax, and Customs authorities. He called for prior consultation with the business community on structural reforms and advocated for a coordinated one-window facilitation mechanism. Ultimately, Mukati emphasized that the primary objective of tax reforms should be to facilitate compliant taxpayers and reduce administrative burdens rather than add new bureaucratic layers.

stories.title: NA Speaker Stresses Stronger Trade and Economic Ties With US
stories.summary:
National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq has underscored the necessity of deepening trade and economic cooperation between Pakistan and the United States, advocating for expanded engagement between the business communities of both nations. He made these remarks during a meeting with a delegation from the American Business Council at Parliament House on Wednesday. Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kiani was also present at the gathering.

Welcoming the delegation, Speaker Sadiq commended the business community for its active role in bolstering Pakistan-United States economic relations. He highlighted that Pakistan provides vast opportunities for trade and investment across multiple sectors, urging stakeholders to explore these avenues through robust business-to-business linkages. Creating a conducive environment for commerce remains a primary priority for the government, which has implemented investor-friendly policies to support corporate partners.

Reaffirming Parliament’s dedication to supporting the private sector, Sadiq assured the visiting delegation of comprehensive legislative cooperation designed to address business concerns and safeguard sectoral interests. He detailed Pakistan’s parliamentary system and legislative procedures, emphasizing Parliament's active role in facilitating commercial activities and maintaining sustained dialogue to consolidate bilateral economic ties. Additionally, the Speaker recognized overseas Pakistanis as a vital national asset capable of driving the country's economic development.

In response, members of the American Business Council delegation thanked Speaker Sadiq for the warm welcome extended at Parliament House. They expressed appreciation for his dedicated interest in resolving commercial issues and fostering a more collaborative environment for foreign and domestic businesses operating within Pakistan.

stories.title: Pakistan Mango Exports Drop 36 Percent Amid Middle East Tensions
stories.summary:
Pakistan's mango exports fell by 36 percent to 78,000 tonnes during the current season, failing to reach the official export target of 80,000 tonnes and leading to a substantial drop in foreign exchange earnings. Waheed Ahmed, Patron-in-Chief of the All Pakistan Fruit and Vegetable Exporters, Importers and Merchants Association (PFVA), reported that the country earned USD 58.5 million this season, a sharp decrease compared to the previous season's volume of 123,000 tonnes and earnings of USD 92.2 million.

The decline was largely driven by ongoing tensions in the Middle East, which restricted demand in key Gulf markets and spiked freight charges. Exports to Gulf nations dropped significantly, with shipments to the UAE and Saudi Arabia, alongside decreases in Qatar and Oman, heavily impacting overall volumes. Furthermore, cross-border trade disruptions and the continued suspension of trade with Afghanistan caused an estimated loss of 24,000 tonnes in export volume.

Despite these challenges, Ahmed noted that commencing exports on June 1, in cooperation with the Ministry of Commerce and the Ministry of National Food Security and Research, helped exporters avoid quality complaints that would have arisen from a May start. However, the domestic industry continues to suffer from climate change impacts, which have reduced overall mango production by about 35 percent from a potential capacity of 1.8 million tonnes. Rising production costs and vulnerable orchards further threaten the sector.

Highlighting mangoes as an essential part of Pakistan's national identity, Ahmed called for federal and provincial government assistance to help growers adopt modern farming techniques. He expressed optimism that exports could recover to previous levels if lasting peace is eventually established in the Middle East region.

stories.title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Government to Launch Subsidized Green Rickshaw Scheme
stories.summary:
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial government is preparing to launch a Green Rickshaw Scheme aimed at providing environmentally friendly and modern public transportation. Asif Rafiq, Advisor to the Governor for Transport, Local Government, Communications and Works, Housing, Agriculture, and Livestock, announced the initiative while chairing a Transport Department meeting in Peshawar on Wednesday. Under the program, eligible citizens will receive rickshaws on four-year easy installments backed by a 50 percent government subsidy to create employment opportunities.

During the meeting, Rafiq also instructed officials of the Peshawar Mass Transit Bus Service to implement a comprehensive strategy to lower administrative and operational expenditures. He set an annual revenue target of Rs 2 billion for the bus service, stressing that financial self-reliance and efficient resource utilization are critical government priorities. Relevant authorities were directed to develop new revenue sources and eliminate corruption to improve public service delivery.

To address urban congestion, Rafiq called for the development of an effective traffic management plan to ease rush-hour commuting problems in Peshawar. He emphasized that modernizing the provincial transport system to make it transparent, eco-friendly, and aligned with citizen needs is an urgent requirement. Senior officials, including Secretary Transport Muhammad Zubair Khan and KP Urban Mobility Authority Managing Director Muhammad Iftikhar, attended the session.

stories.title: FBISE Implements On-the-Spot Question Paper Printing to Stop Leaks
stories.summary:
The Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (FBISE) has introduced an on-the-spot question paper printing system across 35 examination centres during its second annual examinations. According to FBISE Chairman Dr Ikram Ali Malik, the initiative aims to prevent paper leaks while cutting down transportation and bank storage expenses. Under the new system, question papers are shared online 15 minutes before exams begin, and only designated school superintendents and heads can access them using separate passwords to print the required copies.

The board plans to phase out manual bank-based distribution and expand the online printing system to all 1,000 examination centres within a year. A similar online model has operated successfully at foreign centres since 2018. Additionally, the FBISE is consulting institutions to introduce computer-based testing for multiple-choice questions in five major subjects—Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Mathematics, and Computer Science—starting with Class 9 and first-year exams in 2027. This proposed computer testing aims to eliminate human checking errors and deliver same-day results.

Separately, the Higher Education Commission conducted the 35th Law Admission Test through its Education Testing Council. The standardised exam drew 42,547 registered candidates, with over 35,523 individuals appearing at 103 examination centres across 28 cities nationwide to ensure merit-based admissions.

stories.title: SBP Governor Stress That Economic Resilience Requires Consistent Policies and Institutions
stories.summary:
State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmad emphasized on Wednesday that true economic resilience requires more than merely accumulating fiscal and external buffers. Speaking at Standard Chartered Bank’s Annual Global Research Briefing in Karachi, he noted that sustainable stability also depends on consistent, credible policies, flexible markets, and strong institutions capable of effectively responding to emerging global challenges. He pointed out that emerging economies remain especially vulnerable to external shocks, such as geopolitical tensions, commodity price volatility, and climate-induced disruptions.

Highlighting recent macroeconomic performance, Mr Ahmad stated that improved fundamentals have enabled Pakistan to better manage external shocks stemming from the Middle East conflict compared to the intense pressures experienced during the earlier Russia-Ukraine crisis. To permanently break the nation's recurring boom-and-bust cycles, the SBP chief stressed the necessity of boosting exports, increasing domestic savings and investment, and deepening financial markets, while underscoring the vital role of the private sector in driving sustainable growth. He reflected on the difficult monetary tightening, fiscal consolidation, and administrative measures undertaken during fiscal years 2022 and 2023, noting that these steps, backed by multilateral and bilateral partners, successfully restored economic stability and confidence.

Discussing current economic indicators, the SBP governor reported that inflation averaged close to its target range during fiscal year 2026 and is projected to gradually ease toward the medium-term target despite a recent uptick. Furthermore, the current account deficit is anticipated to remain contained within 0 to 1 percent of gross domestic product, while foreign exchange reserves and fiscal buffers continue to strengthen. Real gross domestic product growth reached 3.7 percent in fiscal year 2026 and is expected to exhibit further improvement throughout the current fiscal year, reflecting positive evaluations from international credit rating agencies, foreign investors, and multilateral institutions.

stories.title: Pakistan Cotton Sector Faces Record Price Gap Amid Quality Issues
stories.summary:
Pakistan is experiencing an unprecedented quality crisis in its cotton sector, which has pushed the price differential between low-grade and high-grade lint past a historic Rs3,000 per maund. According to a fortnightly report released by the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association (PCGA) on Wednesday, total nationwide cotton arrivals reached 5.13 million bales by November 15, marking a 5.66 percent increase compared to the 4.85 million bales recorded during the same period last year. However, arrivals during the first half of November slowed down to 388,544 bales, indicating that the season is approaching its conclusion.

Cotton Ginners Forum Chairman Ihsanul Haq explained that severe temperature spikes and environmental pollution caused by sugarcane farming in traditional growing regions have severely impacted fibre quality. This has led to a scarcity of high-grade lint for local textile mills, with domestic prices currently hovering between Rs15,500 and Rs18,500 per maund. Meanwhile, superior-grade cotton from Balochistan has climbed to Rs19,300 per maund. Sajid Mahmood from the Central Cotton Research Institute in Multan added that weather fluctuations have negatively affected crucial fibre traits like staple length and strength.

Across the country, 410 ginning factories remain operational, comprising 203 facilities in Punjab and 207 in Sindh. Sindh registered 2,879,409 bales, with Sanghar generating the highest volume at 1,122,000 bales. Punjab recorded 2,251,765 bales, led by Bahawalnagar with 603,000 bales. Textile mills have procured over 4.44 million bales, while exporters and traders have purchased 98,000 bales, resulting in a total off-take of approximately 4.54 million bales and leaving 590,823 bales of unsold stock.

This severe quality divide matters significantly for Pakistan's domestic textile industry, as it directly shapes manufacturing costs and purchasing strategies. Understanding these supply chain constraints helps stakeholders navigate fluctuating market dynamics and highlights the pressing need to better align local lint standards with industrial demands.

stories.title: SECP Lowers Cost and Cap on Digital Nano Loans
stories.summary:
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has substantially decreased the maximum allowable annual percentage rate (APR) for digital nano-loans. Under new regulations, the APR cap drops from 274 percent to 90 percent for first-time borrowers and to 70 percent for repeat borrowers. This policy change is designed to enhance borrower protections and encourage responsible lending behavior across the financial sector.

As part of these regulatory updates, the SECP is also developing a digital repository for nano-loan borrowers. This database will enable lenders to verify existing liabilities before extending new credit, allowing financial institutions to exercise caution if a customer is already struggling with repayments. The updated rules were formalized through circular no. 26 of 2026, which amends an earlier framework from 2024 to rationalize costs for loans up to Rs50,000 with a maximum repayment duration of 90 days.

The revised caps translate to a maximum daily cost of approximately 0.2466 percent for new borrowers and 0.1918 percent for repeat borrowers. On a Rs10,000 loan, this equates to roughly Rs24.66 and Rs19.18 per day, respectively, encompassing all associated fees such as mark-up, platform charges, and processing fees. By comparison, under the previous 274 percent limit, a 14-day loan would have cost around Rs1,051.

This regulatory intervention matters because it shields vulnerable consumers from exorbitant borrowing costs and predatory debt traps. By capping fees and implementing better cross-lender transparency, the SECP aims to foster a safer environment for digital financial inclusion in Pakistan.

stories.title: US Envoys Expected in Berlin for High-Level Ukraine Discussions
stories.summary:
American diplomatic envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are scheduled to arrive in Berlin on Thursday to engage with Ukrainian representatives and a European negotiating team. A US official confirmed that the discussions aim to intensify international efforts directed at resolving the conflict in Russia and Ukraine. The talks will center on formulating dependable post-war security guarantees for Ukraine, advancing a broad economic recovery strategy, and organizing subsequent rounds of multilateral negotiations.

These diplomatic moves follow recent talks held in Abu Dhabi last week, where Russian, Ukrainian, and US officials convened for the first time in nine months. Following those meetings, Kushner and Witkoff traveled to Moscow to confer with Russian President Vladimir Putin, noting subsequently that European nations would participate in future diplomatic sessions. Although social media statements indicated marginal progress, both sides remain distant from a final settlement, particularly given Russia's desire to secure the Donbas region and Ukraine's reluctance to yield territory.

The discussions in Berlin coincide with US President Donald Trump’s visit to China for a tripartite summit alongside Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. President Trump indicated that the situation in Ukraine would form part of the agenda during the summit. The US official emphasized that the Berlin meetings and the presidential engagements in China form part of a synchronized diplomatic strategy aimed at achieving durable peace.

This diplomatic push is critical as international stakeholders attempt to bridge deep-seated territorial disputes and establish security frameworks for Eastern Europe. Coordinating closely with European and Ukrainian partners underlines the ongoing global efforts to steer warring parties toward formal negotiations.

stories.title: AJK Supreme Court Sets Aside Complete Abolition of Job Quotas
stories.summary:
The Supreme Court of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) has overturned the high court's blanket elimination of regional and refugee quotas in public sector employment. A division bench, consisting of Chief Justice Raja Saeed Akram and Justice Khalid Yousaf Chaudhary, ruled that geographical preferences are not automatically unconstitutional, provided they are backed by statutory law and evidence of under-representation. The court instructed the Public Service Commission (PSC) to restart and conclude all recruitment procedures that had been paused following the high court's August 16, 2025 ruling.

Rather than reinstating previous percentages, the bench ordered the government to conduct a thorough review of existing regional and refugee allocations to ensure compliance with legal and constitutional standards. It also outlined an interim recruitment structure: grades 1 to 7 will be filled via constituency-level competition, grades 8 to 15 at the district level, divisional office vacancies across the division, and senior or state-level positions on open merit among State Subjects. Selections will remain strictly tied to merit, qualifications, and suitability.

In the judgement authored by Chief Justice Akram, the court noted that the AJK Civil Servants Act of 1976 and Civil Servants Rules of 1977 permit provisions for component units and refugees, but stressed that historical quotas cannot continue indefinitely without objective justification. Regarding refugees, the bench clarified that their State Subject status is independent of preferential allocations, meaning the 19 percent quota for 1947 migrants and the 6 percent quota for 1989 migrants cannot be treated as perpetual entitlements without statutory backing. Furthermore, the court ruled that educational admissions must be evaluated separately and set aside high court directives that exceeded AJK's administrative competence.

This ruling is vital for governance and public employment in the region, as it balances the constitutional rights of local candidates and refugees with the principles of merit-based recruitment. By establishing an interim framework and ordering a comprehensive review, the Supreme Court aims to bring legal clarity to public sector hiring.

stories.title: FBR Introduces Proposed Rules for Faceless Income Tax Appeals
stories.summary:
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) released draft rules to establish a faceless income tax appeals framework, removing physical contact between taxpayers and appellate bodies. The system also masks the identities of tax officers ruling on disputes. Notification through SRO 2136 of 2026 amends the Income Tax Rules of 2002 by adding a dedicated chapter for faceless appeals, with final rules anticipated following stakeholder feedback.

Under the proposed guidelines, Commissioners handling appeals via video link remain anonymous, with electronically altered voices preventing identity disclosure. The entire workflow, spanning filings, evidence submission, hearings, and final orders, operates digitally via the FBR’s Iris portal or automated systems. An appeals wing based in Islamabad will house appellate units under the administrative oversight of the FBR’s Member Legal Inland Revenue, while leadership and senior officials are barred from directing commissioners on specific cases.

Virtual proceedings are recorded and archived digitally, and neither taxpayers nor authorized representatives may attend hearings in person, though taxpayers can request decisions based entirely on written arguments. The automated platform can also transfer pending appeals between units to balance workloads and ensure impartiality across the board.

This digital reform matters because it aims to enhance transparency, minimize corruption risks, and streamline tax dispute resolution in Pakistan. By modernizing administrative procedures through automation, the FBR seeks to build greater trust within the tax system.

stories.title: Israeli Forces Kill Three Palestinians During Fresh Gaza Push
stories.summary:
Israeli tanks pushed into the central Gaza Strip on Wednesday, with military officials stating operations target Hamas infrastructure outside areas under Israeli control. Witnesses reported tanks moving onto the primary Salahudeen road west of the Yellow Line, marking the boundary of territory still held by Israel despite a year-long ceasefire. Palestinian medics reported that an Israeli airstrike near the military raid killed one person, while separate strikes earlier in the day killed two others in Deir al-Balah and Gaza City.

The ongoing military actions occur alongside a newly released report by the Board of Peace, overseen by US President Donald Trump. The 12-page United Nations Security Council report accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to honor commitments to end the conflict, leaving Gaza's population in severe conditions and threatening the ceasefire's survival. The board noted that the gap between agreed terms and ground realities poses the primary risk to the peace process. Hamas official Basem Naim rejected the report as disinformation, alleging the board shields Israel from accountability.

More than two million Palestinians remain confined to roughly one-third of Gaza, primarily residing in makeshift tents and damaged structures. The report criticized the Israeli government for delaying decisions on training a civilian Palestinian police force and noted that Israeli-imposed restrictions on supplies, alongside funding shortages, have worsened conditions ahead of seasonal flooding.

These developments matter because ongoing military incursions and stalled political implementation threaten to collapse the fragile ceasefire, deepening the humanitarian crisis for millions of displaced Palestinians. Monitoring compliance by both sides remains essential for international stability efforts in the region.

stories.title: Kuwait and regional US allies targeted in fresh Iranian drone strikes
stories.summary:
Tensions in the Middle East escalated significantly after Iran stated it targeted US drone and missile installations at Kuwait's Ali Al Salem base. The overnight operation marks Tehran's first direct attack on the US-allied Gulf nation since September, following a recent American strike on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

Alongside the incident in Kuwait, regional security faced multiple disruptions as Bahrain intercepted its third aerial attack of the week. Meanwhile, a Saudi-led coalition successfully intercepted and destroyed a Houthi cruise missile heading toward Riyadh, which triggered a loud explosion across the Saudi capital that left residents without prior phone warnings.

Maritime security also deteriorated further when UAE state oil firm ADNOC reported that a crew member went missing after their vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz. While eleven other crew members sustained injuries and received medical care, ongoing search and rescue operations continued. In response to these maritime hazards, US Central Command issued an advisory warning that military action could be taken against any vessel attempting to evade the blockade by receiving cargo at sea from ships loaded in Iranian ports.

Amidst these developments, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio downplayed intelligence assessments concerning potential threats to Washington, stating in Manila that he saw no imminent danger. The diplomatic and military friction follows earlier calls from Gulf states urging a return to dialogue, even as leaders like Kuwait's crown prince explore mediation efforts with Pakistan.

stories.title: Islamabad Police Pledge Enhanced Security and Cooperation to Business Community
stories.summary:
Islamabad Police met with local traders and industrialists on Wednesday to address their concerns, reinforce security protocols, and streamline grievance resolution. Held at the Islamabad Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ICCI), the interactive session was led by SSP Operations Captain Ali Raza Qazi (R), alongside ICCI President Mohammad Zikria Akbar Zia, Senior Vice President Mohammad Ashfaq Hussain Chatha, and Police Committee Chairman Saif ur Rehman Khan.

The police administration recognized the business community as a vital pillar for economic stability and growth. During the meeting, officials promised to resolve police-related complaints promptly at the local station level to eliminate procedural hurdles and reduce delays. Furthermore, authorities announced plans to formulate comprehensive Standard Operating Procedures to assist complainants dealing with lost property documents.

As part of institutional cooperation, the police assured that ICCI would receive formal representation in the Alternative Dispute Resolution mechanism. Both police officials and chamber leaders emphasized that consistent engagement between the two institutions is necessary to foster investor confidence, protect commercial activities, and maintain a secure business atmosphere in the region.

The session concluded with the presentation of relevant appointment letters to members of the ICCI Police Committee. Participants highlighted that regular communication will enable both sides to identify emerging challenges proactively and develop practical, business-friendly policing solutions to support sustainable economic development.

stories.title: PTI leaders resolve internal rifts and demand medical care for Imran Khan
stories.summary:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and senior lawyer Sardar Latif Khosa publicly dismissed rumors of internal discord outside the Islamabad High Court. The leaders shook hands to project party unity, with Mr. Khosa referring to Mr. Raja as his junior, following earlier speculation regarding differing approaches toward engaging with the establishment.

During the media appearance, Mr. Raja emphasized that party members remain united behind founding chairman Imran Khan and that all strategic decisions strictly follow his directions. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan similarly affirmed that the party does not believe in power-sharing arrangements and operates solely under the incarcerated leader's guidelines.

Parallel to these political developments, the PTI formally delivered a 44-page letter to the Adiala jail administration. The party strongly criticized authorities for allegedly defying Supreme Court directives by taking Mr. Khan to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) instead of transferring him to Shifa International Hospital for necessary medical treatment.

In a related legal proceeding, the Islamabad High Court granted Barrister Salman Safdar seven days to prepare arguments regarding the convictions of Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi in the Al-Qadir Trust case. The court additionally instructed prison authorities to ensure hygienic conditions, proper medical facilities, and a specialist examination for Bushra Bibi in accordance with jail rules.

stories.title: UBG President Calls for Industrial Policies to Strengthen Pakistan's Economy
stories.summary:
United Business Group President Zubair Tufail stated on Wednesday that the government must implement practical measures to promote trade and industry in order to place Pakistan's economy on sustainable foundations. Speaking in Karachi, Tufail emphasized that strong representation from the business sector within the Federation is essential to deliver constructive policy suggestions regarding long-term economic continuity, industrial expansion, and investment.

Tufail highlighted the upcoming Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry elections for the 2027-2028 term. He expressed strong confidence that UBG's presidential candidate, SM Tanveer, will secure a heavy majority, noting that the candidate enjoys widespread backing from various industrial and trading circles. According to Tufail, a strong leadership team is necessary to help guide the country toward economic stability and ensure effective recommendations reach government officials.

The UBG president underscored that private-sector consultation and close coordination with the government are critical tools for overcoming ongoing financial challenges. He stressed that prioritizing business-friendly policies will encourage both domestic and foreign investors to commit capital to the country.

Concluding his remarks, Tufail reiterated that the United Business Group remains committed to resolving the grievances of traders and industrialists. He called on all economic stakeholders to collaborate closely to improve Pakistan's financial standing and achieve lasting economic growth.

stories.title: Pakistan Prepares First National Youth Policy Following 41-Point Charter Demand
stories.summary:
The federal government plans to launch Pakistan's first National Adolescent and Youth Policy in the coming months. This development follows the presentation of a 41-point charter by young leaders, who are urging federal and provincial institutions to transform their proposals into legislation, policy reforms, and dedicated budgets within two years. The announcement was made by Rana Mashhood Ahmad Khan, Chairman of the Prime Minister’s Youth Programme, during the National Youth Summit 2026 in Islamabad. The summit was organized by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute, UNFPA Pakistan, and the Prime Minister’s Youth Programme.

The upcoming policy will target three distinct age cohorts, covering individuals aged 10-15, 15-19, and 19-29 years to ensure age-appropriate interventions. Government initiatives already underway include the National Youth Employment Policy, which seeks at least 35 percent annual female workforce participation and aims for young entrepreneurs to account for 10 percent of new company registrations yearly. Additionally, Rs292 billion has been allocated under the Prime Minister’s Youth Business and Agriculture Loan Scheme for loans ranging from Rs500,000 to Rs25 million, while nearly one million youth have registered on the Digital Youth Hub alongside roughly 2,400 companies.

The youth-led charter demands sweeping reforms across education, employment, entrepreneurship, healthcare, climate financing, data protection, and political representation. Key demands include emergency frameworks for green skills training in renewable energy, paid internships by December 2027, expanded incubation centers, venture capital ecosystems, and mandatory life-skills-based education by 2028. Climate-related demands call for channeling carbon levy proceeds—which have reached about Rs70 billion compared to a Ministry of Climate Change budget of Rs2 billion—toward environmental resilience rather than the Federal Consolidated Fund, alongside directing carbon credit revenues from mangrove forests to local protection communities.

Furthermore, young participants requested reserved seats for youth in the National Assembly, Senate, and local governments, alongside robust data protection and privacy legislation. Senator Jan Muhammad Buledi and Amna Batool assured attendees that these recommendations would be shared with the Prime Minister's Office and parliament for serious consideration. SDPI Board of Governors Chairman Shafqat Kakakhel emphasized the urgency of engaging the country's population under 30 in structured policy decisions to secure Pakistan's development future.

stories.title: Dar and Malik Discuss Pakistan's Participation in Delhi SCO Dialogue
stories.summary:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar met with Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination Dr Musadik Masood Malik in Islamabad on Wednesday. The two officials discussed Pakistan's upcoming participation in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilization Dialogue.

The international event is scheduled to take place in New Delhi from November 20 to 22, 2026. During the discussions, Senator Dar reaffirmed Pakistan's dedication to its responsibilities as the current Chair of the Council of Heads of States of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.

The Foreign Minister emphasized that Pakistan remains firmly committed to advancing collaborative efforts among member states. He also noted the importance of promoting cultural exchanges and strengthening people-to-people ties across the region during the dialogue.

stories.title: Czech Ambassador Visits Peshawar to Explore Bilateral Economic Cooperation
stories.summary:
Ladislav Steinhübel, the Ambassador of the Czech Republic to Pakistan, traveled to Peshawar on Wednesday alongside Political Counsellor Zdeněk Koudelka. The visit was arranged to examine avenues for boosting trade, industrial collaboration, and investment, specifically focusing on Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Barrister Assad Saifullah Khan, the Honorary Consul General of the Czech Republic in Peshawar, hosted the delegation.
